content.title: Photos: 2026 French Quarter Fest kicks off - Verite News New Orleans
content.text: A second line down Bourbon Street kicks off the 2026 French Quarter Festival on Thursday, April 16. Credit: Christiana Botic/Verite News and Catchlight Local/Report for America Audio recording is automated for accessibility. Humans wrote and edited the story. The 2026 French Quarter Festival kicked off Thursday morning with a lively second-line parade down Bourbon Street and ending at Jackson Square, where the festival opened the gates to the public. Lines immediately formed for food and drinks in the square while Preservation Brass took to the NewOrleans.com Stage to start the festival. Eris Bill, an Ocean Springs native now living in Richmond, Va., woke up early to start her morning with the second line. It’s her first year attending the festival, and she says she’s most looking forward to seeing John Boutté, Mahogany Hall All Stars and headliner PJ Morton. The French Quarter Festival second line rolls down Bourbon Street. Credit: Christiana Botic/Verite News and Catchlight Local/Report for America Louisiana State Museum employee Latrice Dillon didn’t have to travel quite as far — just a few steps out the museum door — to enjoy the festival’s offerings.“I’m excited about all the vendors, the food,” she said, adding that she wants to try Chicken’s Kitchen, a new addition to the fest’s food lineup. This year’s festival boasts 70 local vendors, over 300 performances across 20 stages, and an expanded riverfront experience at the recently opened Goldring Woldenberg Riverfront Park at Governor Nicholls Wharf. While exploring the brand new park, festival-goers can catch performances at the Pan-American Life Insurance Group Stage and the Jack Daniel’s Stage. Headliners include beloved New Orleans artists PJ Morton, Irma Thomas, Cyril Neville and Big Freedia. The free festival continues through Sunday, April 19. Sierra Green and the Giants play on the Jack Daniels Stage. Credit: Christiana Botic/Verite News and Catchlight Local/Report for America Visitors dance at the Pan-American Life Insurance Group Stage, located on the recently opened Goldring Woldenberg Riverfront Park at Governor Nicholls Wharf.
